statement: Public Anangu/heritage descriptions present Tjukurpa as a continuing law, knowledge, and spiritual-philosophical framework in which ancestral beings shaped the landscape and established responsibilities governing relationships among people, land, plants, animals, water, ceremony, and social life.

sources.citation: Australian Government, Uluru–Kata Tjuta National Park World Heritage description, updated 16 Apr. 2026.
Australian Government, Uluru–Kata Tjuta National Park — Park management: Tjukurpa and management, updated 4 Mar. 2026.

notes: Placed in the product's supernatural/cosmological comparison bucket only to support cross-cultural UI comparison. The record itself preserves the sources' broader categories of law, philosophy, spirituality, knowledge, and landscape responsibility.
